title: The split formula, offshoots, and a counterexample to Claim B for arrangements in general
claim: Lemma C: bonds of the next junction graph are families of disjoint non-adjacent old bonds glued by new junctions, with the cost |delta(S)| + sum over inside new junctions of f + |P\S| - |P cap S|. Lemma O: offshoots never change least bonds through old pairs; offshoot-only rounds extend any isometry keeping loose per live junction. Proposition X: a 7-junction connected arrangement whose table symmetry keeps the round reading but does not extend (Claim B false for arrangements in general; not a reached stage).
standard_statement: Splitting a vertex of a graph: cocircuits of the split graph from families of cocircuits of the original plus new vertices, with a discount formula; pendant new vertices preserve least cocircuits; cocircuit-distance isometries preserving the attachment need not extend.
